d: Alexia Putellas and the 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or are at the centre of a debate about how women’s football is recognised on its biggest stage. While Harry Kane’s 2026 Ballon d’Or win has put the men’s award in the spotlight, the women’s ceremony has raised questions about unequal attention and representation. From a men’s football montage featuring Michael Owen to the number of journalists voting for the women’s award, the concerns go beyond the ceremony itself. Women’s football continues to grow through the Women’s Champions League and international tournaments but does that progress…
